hints: Focus on what temperature really means for molecules, it increases their average kinetic energy.
Remember that with the same total number of molecules, if energies spread out more widely the peak must drop and shift to the right.
Think about the area under the curve to the right of $E_a$, that area shows the fraction able to react and it grows when heated.
walkthrough:
**Recall what the Boltzmann curve shows**

Think of this curve as showing how energy is shared out. Most molecules have moderate energy near peak P, a few have very low energy and a few have very high energy.

The total area under the curve is fixed because the total number of molecules (1 mole) does not change.

**Apply the effect of higher temperature**

Heating gives molecules more energy on average. So the whole distribution spreads out toward higher energy.

Because the same area must now cover a wider range, the peak P gets lower and moves slightly to the right. The curve flattens and extends further along the energy axis.

**Link to activation energy**

Only molecules with energy $> E_a$ can react. That is the small area under the curve to the right of $E_a$.

When the curve flattens and shifts right, that tail area gets bigger. So more molecules can overcome $E_a$, which is why rate increases with temperature.

options.A: Incorrect. The peak does not get higher on heating. A higher, narrower peak would mean energies are less spread out, which is the effect of cooling, not heating. Fewer molecules over $E_a$ is also opposite to the true effect.
options.B: Incorrect. It is true that more molecules will have energy $> E_a$ on heating, but the peak will not be higher. Students sometimes think higher temperature just lifts the whole curve up, but total area must stay constant so a wider spread means a lower peak.
options.C: Incorrect. The first half is right, the peak P will be lower, but the second half is wrong. Heating increases, not decreases, the proportion with energy $> E_a$. This option confuses the lower peak with fewer successful molecules.
options.D: Correct. Higher temperature spreads the distribution to higher energies, so the peak P lowers and flattens to keep total area constant, while the area beyond $E_a$ increases. That means more molecules have energy $> E_a$ and can react.
